$comment: PROVENANCE MANIFEST for every non-JS binary payload shipped in the installer.
This file is the answer to 'where did that binary come from?'. A blob of unknown
origin in a repository is unacceptable, and licence matters: ghostscript was
rejected for this pipeline because it is AGPL. Every entry therefore records a
source URL, a version, a licence, and a SHA-256 — of the ARCHIVE as fetched and
of each FILE extracted from it.
BUILD TIME ONLY. `npm run payloads` reads this file on a DEVELOPER's machine and
populates the gitignored resources/ tree; electron-builder then bakes that tree
into the installer. The APPLICATION never reads this file and never fetches
anything — CLAUDE.md §2 requires it to run with networking disabled, and
`npm run verify:offline` enforces that no payload URL survives into the bundle.
Hashes were each cross-checked against the publisher's OWN checksum manifest
(qpdf's qpdf-12.3.2.sha256, sqlite-vec's checksums.txt) rather than trusting the
bytes this machine happened to receive. See docs/packaging.md §Payloads.
A pinned SHA-256 protects against a re-uploaded release asset, a poisoned cache
and a corrupted transfer. It does NOT protect against an upstream project that
was compromised before it published. That residual risk is accepted and named
here rather than left implicit.

payloads.purpose: PDF linearization/recompression for the `optimize` pipeline stage.
payloads.degradation: The optimize stage reports `skipped` naming the missing binary; documents are stored unoptimized. No output is silently changed.
payloads.notice: qpdf is Apache-2.0. Apache-2.0 §4(d) requires the NOTICE to be reproduced; a third-party-licences screen is owed before release.

$comment: BUILT FROM SOURCE, not fetched. The upstream binary release
qpdf-12.3.2-bin-linux-x86_64.zip ships a private gnutls/nettle/p11-kit/idn2
TLS stack in lib/ (verified: ldd resolves libgnutls.so.30 out of the zip).
Shipping that would mean signing, notarizing and tracking CVEs for a whole
TLS implementation inside an app that never opens a socket. The static
musl build links libc/libstdc++ only.
TWO hashes are pinned. `source.sha256` is the input tarball, immutable
and independently published by upstream. `files[].sha256` is the BUILT
binary — which is safe to pin because this build was measured to be
bit-reproducible: a second `docker build --no-cache` from the same pinned
base-image digest produced a byte-identical 4658408-byte binary with the
same SHA-256. That is why the base image is pinned by DIGEST and not by
the `alpine:3.21` tag, which is rebuilt for every CVE patch and would
silently change the toolchain and therefore the output.
Honest limit: reproducibility was confirmed on ONE host. A different
Docker/BuildKit version could still perturb the output. If the hash below
ever mismatches, that is a signal to investigate the toolchain — not to
edit the number until it passes.

files.attributes: statically linked (musl), crypto=native, stripped, zero network symbols

$comment: Fetched, not built: the mingw64 release contains ONLY qpdf.exe, qpdf30.dll
and three mingw runtime DLLs — no TLS stack — so the objection that forced
a source build on Linux does not apply. The DLLs must sit BESIDE the exe.
The other ~40 MB of that zip (headers, static libs, docs) is not shipped.
WASM, because nobody publishes a macOS qpdf binary and this repo has no macOS
build host. Upstream v12.3.2 ships linux-x86_64, mingw32/64, msvc32/64, an
AppImage and source — nothing for darwin — so the choice on a Mac is a wasm
qpdf or no optimize stage at all.
The SAME qpdf, compiled to wasm, which is what makes it admissible here. The
optimize stage is a transformer of document.file@v1 and every evidence-span
highlight is anchored to item geometry, which is why ghostscript was rejected
(it moved geometry in 19 of 20 papers). Measured before adopting this:
qpdf-wasm and the native binary were run over 6 real papers with identical
arguments and the output compared through the same pdfjs the viewer anchors
against — 33,090 text items, 0 moved, 0 text differences.
VERSION SKEW IS DELIBERATE AND MUST STAY VISIBLE: this is qpdf 12.2.0 while
the native payload is 12.3.2, because the wasm package pins its own qpdf. The
optimize stage folds the flavour AND the version into its fingerprint
(`qpdf|wasm|12.2.0` vs `qpdf|12.3.2`) so a Mac that later gains a native
binary re-runs rather than serving a cached verdict from the other tool.
ONE payload for both architectures: wasm is architecture-independent, so the
x64 and arm64 entries are byte-identical by construction rather than by
coincidence. Both are listed anyway because electron-builder filters
bin/darwin-${arch}/** per architecture.
ISC-licensed packaging around Apache-2.0 qpdf; both notices are owed on the
third-party-licences screen.

payloads.purpose: Tesseract English model for the `ocr` stage (scanned PDFs only). `best` rather than `fast` because scientific notation is where the fast model loses: a plus-minus read as `6`, a superscript minus as `2 1`.
payloads.degradation: The ocr stage reports `skipped`. It must NEVER fall back to the CDN: tesseract.js downloads eng.traineddata from jsdelivr when `langPath` is unset (verified twice), which would break the offline rule. With langPath local and the file absent it fails loudly with ENOENT — keep it that way.

all.$comment: Platform-independent data. Pinned to the 4.1.0 TAG rather than a branch, so the bytes cannot move under the recorded hash.

payloads.purpose: Semantic search. Snowflake arctic-embed-s, int8 ONNX, 384-dim, CLS pooling — chosen by measurement over this repo's own corpus (tmp/embedding-model-decision.md §5).
payloads.degradation: Search falls back to keyword/FTS and MUST say so on the results surface. A semantic search that silently returns keyword results is the worst outcome available: the user reads a ranked list and concludes the corpus holds nothing relevant.

$comment: Pinned to a REVISION SHA, not to `main`. Model cards are silently
re-uploaded, and a model id alone is not a version — §7 of the decision
doc requires model_revision on every stored vector precisely because
changing weights invalidates every embedding in the index.
The directory layout is dictated by @huggingface/transformers, which with
env.localModelPath=<resources>/models resolves <org>/<model>/<file> and
<org>/<model>/onnx/<file>. Do not flatten it.

payloads.purpose: Project relevance. cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2, int8 ONNX — a cross-encoder reads the project description and a paper together and emits one relevance logit, which is a judgement the embedding model cannot make because it never sees the two texts at the same time.
payloads.degradation: The rerank stage reports `skipped` naming the missing model and relevance is left NULL — never 0, which would draw an empty bar reading as `judged, and found irrelevant`.

$comment: A SIBLING ROOT of models/, not a subdirectory of it. discoverModelId()
in src/main/embedding/space.ts THROWS when it finds a second directory
carrying an onnx/ folder under modelsDir(), so one root per ROLE keeps
'exactly one model lives here' a structural fact rather than an
exclusion list somebody has to remember to extend.
RENAMED ON THE WAY IN. Upstream calls the int8 weights
onnx/model_qint8_avx512.onnx; quantizationOf() matches
_quantized|_fp16|_int8|_uint8|_q4 and falls through to 'fp32' for
anything else, so under its upstream name this file would be recorded
as fp32 provenance AND loaded with dtype:'fp32'. The local name is the
one the code can read honestly.
Pinned to a REVISION SHA for the same reason the embedding model is:
a model id is not a version, and re-uploaded weights change every
score the corpus was ranked by.

payloads.purpose: Vector k-NN over embeddings, as a SQLite loadable extension (better-sqlite3 loadExtension).
payloads.degradation: Vector search reports unavailable; search falls back to keyword/FTS with the same disclosure the embedding model requires.
$comment: Taken from the GitHub release rather than the npm package so that ONE
manifest-and-hash mechanism governs every payload, and so the darwin and
win32 artifacts can be provisioned from this Linux host.
ARCH IS IN THE PATH. macOS ships separate x64 and arm64 builds and upstream
publishes a distinct dylib for each; a platform-only path would load the
wrong one on half of all Macs.
